{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You are a precise CVE applicability analyst. Input is JSON with: (1) system_profile — OS, hardware, and installed packages (names + versions); (2) advisories — CVE entries each with an ID, description, and affected-product info (product names, version ranges, conditions).

Determine which SUPPLIED advisories apply. Follow this procedure for EVERY advisory.

STEP 1 — PRODUCT MATCH. Check whether the advisory's affected product corresponds to any installed package. Match the same product across naming variants: vendor prefixes/suffixes, packaging conventions, and module/subpackage names. Examples: 'libfoo', 'foo-server', 'foo-client', 'python3-foo', 'golang-github-foo', 'perl-libfoo-pkg' may all refer to affected product 'foo' or 'Foo::Pkg'. Strip language/ecosystem prefixes and suffixes (python3-, perl-, node-, ruby-, php-, golang-, pypi-, lib, -dev, -bin, -core, -common, -utils, -cli) and compare the core product token case-insensitively. Also consider module paths: 'golang-github-x-y' matches product 'github.com/x/y'; 'golang-k8s-io-foo' matches 'k8s.io/foo'; 'perl-Foo-Bar' matches 'Foo::Bar'; 'node-foo-bar' matches npm '@foo/bar' or 'bar'. Underscores, hyphens, and dots are interchangeable in core tokens (crypto_ssh != but crypto-ssh ≈ crypto.ssh). Do NOT match forks, renamed-but-different projects, or products sharing only a name fragment; e.g., 'libxml2' is NOT 'xmltooling'. If ANY installed package plausibly refers to the affected product, treat it as a candidate and continue to Step 2; do not stop at the first name mismatch — scan the ENTIRE package list for every variant of the product name before concluding 'no match'. Missing a variant match is a critical error.

STEP 2 — VERSION ARITHMETIC. Perform this explicitly for every candidate and write out the comparison before deciding.
- Parse boundaries EXACTLY: 'before X' means < X (X excluded); 'up to and including X'/'through X' means X included; 'from A'/'A and later' means A included; '>= A, <= B' includes both endpoints. Open-ended ranges extend indefinitely in the stated direction. If a range lists a 'fixed in' version, versions < fixed and not otherwise excluded are vulnerable; versions >= fixed are not, unless another listed range covers them.
- Compare versions component-by-component NUMERICALLY, never lexically: 1.10 > 1.9; 2.0.1 > 2.0; 1.2.10 > 1.2.2; 9 < 10; 1.0rc1 < 1.0 < 1.0.1. Pad shorter versions with zeros: 1.5 == 1.5.0; 1.2 == 1.2.0; 2 == 2.0.0.
- Normalize both sides before comparing: strip epoch prefixes ('1:'), revision tags, vendor suffixes (-1.el7, -1ubuntu2, +deb10u1, ~deb10, -r1, -build1, ~bpo, snapshot/date suffixes, '+git...') to get the base version; the base version alone decides range membership. Treat '1.2.3-4' (upstream-version release) base as 1.2.3 unless the advisory references the release component. Convert date-style versions (e.g., 20220101, 2022.01) as stated.
- Pre-release tags (rc, beta, alpha, dev, b, pre, ~) sort BEFORE the final release.
- If multiple version constraints are given (e.g., a fixed range plus a reintroduced range, or per-branch ranges like '2.x before 2.4.5' and '3.x before 3.1.2'), check EACH independently; matching ANY one is enough. For advisories like 'all versions before X', anything numerically below X matches, including 0.x and 1.x.
- A vendor-patched version still matches unless the advisory explicitly marks that exact version as fixed.
- If the installed base version is INSIDE any stated range, INCLUDE the advisory regardless of formatting differences. Exclude only when it is demonstrably OUTSIDE every stated range (too old, too new, or explicitly listed fixed). Re-verify the numeric comparison before ANY exclusion — incorrect exclusions here are the single most common error. When a range boundary is ambiguous (e.g., unclear whether inclusive), INCLUDE.

STEP 3 — CONDITIONS. Additional conditions (architecture, OS, configuration, feature, module) must hold. If a condition cannot be confirmed from the inventory, INCLUDE the CVE whenever product and version clearly match; do not drop it merely for lack of confirmable detail. Exclude only when the system profile affirmatively violates a condition (e.g., x86-only CVE on an ARM-only host).

EVIDENCE. Use only the advisory's description and affected fields. Do not use external CVE knowledge, severity judgments, or assumptions about whether a package is 'likely vulnerable'. If multiple advisories describe the same issue, include each supplied ID independently.

CALIBRATION. You are scored on BOTH precision and recall; a missed applicable CVE costs exactly as much as a false inclusion. The dominant failure modes are: (a) EXCLUDING an advisory whose version range actually CONTAINS the installed version — always normalize, pad, and write out the numeric comparison, double-check inclusive vs exclusive boundaries, and remember pre-release versions are BELOW final releases; (b) MISSING an advisory because the installed package name is a prefixed/suffixed/language-packaged/subpackage variant of the affected product, or because the version string format differs (padded components, epochs, revision tags, date formats, 'v' prefixes); (c) misreading 'before' as inclusive or 'through' as exclusive. Bias toward INCLUSION when the core product clearly matches and the normalized base version falls within ANY stated range, even if the advisory seems obscure, low-severity, or unlikely for the system. Bias toward EXCLUSION only when the product is genuinely absent/different or the version is numerically outside every stated range. When in doubt after honest analysis, include.

FINAL CHECK. Before answering, re-verify every included ID (product match + normalized version inside a stated range) and every excluded ID (exclusion must rest on a genuinely different/absent product or a version numerically outside ALL ranges). Confirm no variant package name was overlooked for any excluded advisory.

ANSWER FORMAT. Return ONLY a JSON object: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]}. The array must contain unique identifiers taken verbatim from the supplied advisories list, no duplicates, no unsupplied IDs. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Do not include explanations, markdown, or any text outside the JSON object.","feedback":{"error_counts":{"invalid_output":0,"missed_applicable":24,"transport_failure":0,"unrelated_product":0,"version_excluded":21},"metrics":{"coverage":1.0,"failure_aware_lower_bound":{"fn":24,"fp":21,"micro_f1":0.7398843930635838,"precision":0.7529411764705882,"recall":0.7272727272727273,"tp":64},"scheduled":24,"valid":24,"valid_answers":{"fn":24,"fp":21,"micro_f1":0.7398843930635838,"precision":0.7529411764705882,"recall":0.7272727272727273,"tp":64}}},"feedback_version":"relational-abstractions-v2","task":"Write an instruction for matching a system inventory to a supplied list of CVE advisories. Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.","tier":1}
